verses.text: This is the teaching about the guilt offering. It is most holy.
The guilt offering must be killed in the place where the burnt offering is killed. Its blood will be splashed all around the altar.
All its fat will be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the inside parts,
the two kidneys with the fat on them near the lower back, and the fatty covering of the liver, removed with the kidneys.
The priest will burn them on the altar as a gift made by fire to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
Any male among the priests may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering. The same rule is for both. It belongs to the priest who makes people right with God with it.
The priest who offers someone's burnt offering may keep the skin of that animal for himself.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, or cooked in a pot or on a flat pan, belongs to the priest who offers it.
And every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all of Aaron's sons, shared equally.
This is the teaching about the peace offering that someone brings to the LORD:
If he brings it to say thank you, he must offer with it flat bread made without yeast and mixed with oil, thin wafers without yeast spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour well mixed with oil.
Along with his thank offering, he must also bring loaves of bread made with yeast.
He must give one of each kind as a special gift to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offering.
The meat of the thank offering must be eaten on the day it is offered. None of it may be left until morning.
But if his offering is to keep a promise, or is a gift he chose freely to give, it must be eaten on the day he offers it, and what is left may be eaten the next day.
But any meat still left on the third day must be burned in the fire.

If any of the meat of the peace offering is eaten on the third day, the offering will not be accepted, and it will not count for the person who brought it. It will be disgusting, and whoever eats it will carry the blame.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten. It must be burned in the fire. As for other meat, anyone who is clean may eat it.
But if someone who is unclean eats meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.

If someone touches anything unclean, whether something unclean from a person, or an unclean animal, or any unclean disgusting thing, and then eats meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: Do not eat any fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.
The fat of an animal that died by itself, or was killed by wild animals, may be used for other things, but you must never eat it.
Anyone who eats the fat of an animal that may be offered as a gift made by fire to the LORD must be cut off from his people.
Wherever you live, do not eat any blood, whether from a bird or an animal.
Anyone who eats any blood must be cut off from his people."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: Whoever brings a peace offering to the LORD must bring part of it as a special gift to the LORD.
He must bring the gifts made by fire to the LORD with his own hands. He must bring the fat together with the breast, and the breast will be waved in front of the LORD as a wave offering.
The priest will burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
Give the right thigh of your peace offerings to the priest as a special gift.
The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the peace offering will have the right thigh as his share.

From the peace offerings of the people of Israel, I have taken the breast that is waved and the thigh that is lifted up, and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons. This is their share from the people of Israel forever."
This is the share set apart for Aaron and his sons from the gifts made by fire to the LORD, from the day they were brought forward to serve the LORD as priests.
On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded the people of Israel to give them this. It is their share forever, for all their families to come.
This is the teaching about the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the offering for making priests, and the peace offering.
The LORD gave these commands to Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the people of Israel to bring their offerings to the LORD in the Sinai desert.
